title: Contagious Effects of a Political Intervention in Debt Contracts: Evidence Using Loan-Level Data
abstract: Using an unexpected government regulation that restricted the ability of microfinance institutions to recover loans in one Indian state, I examine whether this intervention affected bank loan performance. The bank loan delinquency rate significantly increased as a result. In response, the ex post bank credit supply declined by more than half. For identification, I compare loans from branches located in regions subject to this intervention with loans from nearby branches of the same bank located in regions not subject to the intervention. I conclude that political interventions in credit markets could have significant spillover effects. Received October 29, 2016; editorial decision November 28, 2017 by Editor Philip Strahan. Authors have furnished an Internet Appendix, which is available on the Oxford University Press Web site next to the link to the final published paper online.

summary.oneLiner: A sudden Indian state rule limiting microfinance loan recovery was followed by higher bank loan delinquency and a drop in credit supply of over half.
summary.overview: The paper studies what happened to bank lending after an unexpected government regulation limited how microfinance institutions could recover loans in one Indian state. Loan delinquency (borrowers falling behind on payments) rose significantly at banks. Banks then reduced their ex post credit supply (the amount they lent after the intervention) by more than half. The author concludes that political interventions in credit markets could have significant spillover effects, meaning effects that reach beyond the directly regulated lenders.
summary.question: Did a government intervention restricting microfinance loan recovery in one Indian state affect the performance of bank loans and bank credit supply?
summary.method: The author compares loans from bank branches in regions subject to the intervention with loans from nearby branches of the same bank in regions not subject to it. The abstract does not give further estimation details.
summary.data: Loan-level data on bank loans from Indian bank branches. The abstract does not state the sample size or time period.
findings: The bank loan delinquency rate significantly increased as a result of the intervention.
In response, ex post bank credit supply declined by more than half.
The author concludes that political interventions in credit markets could have significant spillover effects.
summary.whyItMatters: The paper suggests that policymakers who intervene in credit markets should expect spillover effects that reach banks, not only the lenders directly regulated. The abstract does not spell out specific managerial or investor actions.
geographies: India (one Indian state, not named in the abstract)
